title: US policy rates, daily (2007-2026), percent: effective federal funds rate, FOMC target and target range, interest on reserves, overnight reverse repo award rate
source: Federal Reserve Bank of New York (effective federal funds rate; overnight reverse repo award rate) and Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (target rate and range; interest on required, excess and reserve balances), via FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
series: EFFR (effective federal funds rate); DFEDTAR (target, to 2008-12-15); DFEDTARU and DFEDTARL (upper and lower limits of the target range, from 2008-12-16); IOER and IORR (interest on excess and on required reserves, 2008-10-09 to 2021-07-28); IORB (interest on reserve balances, from 2021-07-29); RRPONTSYAWARD (overnight reverse repurchase agreements award rate, Treasury securities sold by the Federal Reserve in temporary open market operations)
license: The Board's rates are works of the US government. The New York Fed's terms of use (https://www.newyorkfed.org/privacy/termsofuse, read 2026-10-14) allow its content to be copied and distributed with its source identifiers; for reference rates such as the EFFR they require this notice wherever the data are presented: 'The Effective Federal Funds Rate is subject to the Terms of Use posted at newyorkfed.org. The New York Fed is not responsible for publication of the Effective Federal Funds Rate by this project, does not sanction or endorse any particular republication, and has no liability for your use.' Chapter 4 prints the notice in the caption of the figure that shows the EFFR. FRED's terms ask users to 'cite the data source and acknowledge that you obtained the data from FRED' (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/legal/; quoted in fred_prices_monthly.json).
notes: Downloaded 2026-10-14; the snapshot keeps every date from 2007-01-01 on which at least one series has a value (target rates are given on weekends, market rates on business days only). SOFR is not included: the New York Fed's terms add a licence notice for the data DTCC provides for it, and the chapter quotes its September 2019 values from the Federal Reserve's FEDS Note instead.
